\section*{Score-I papers}
\begin{bankq}[id=SI03-P1-PHY-S1-Q05, source={Score-I - Test 03 (07 Jan 2022)}, paper=1, qno=5, type=multi, subtopic={Relative motion}, answer={A,B,C}, answer_src=key, difficulty=8, diff_parts={K2 S3 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: pursuit problem, a lion chasing a person in a circular arena | steps: lion always runs toward the person; relative motion with angular speeds; chase along circles; condition for safety; check | I: pursuit geometry in a circular arena}]
Poor Dinanath (D) is thrown into a circular arena of radius $a$ containing a lion (L). Initially the lion is at the centre O of the arena while Dinanath is at $(a,0)$. Dinanath decides to run at his maximum speed $u$ around the perimeter. The lion responds by running at its maximum speed $v$ in such a way that it remains on the (moving) radius OD. Choose the correct statement(s).
\bfig{94.2}{SI03_p1_phy_s1_q05_1.png}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{During the chase, distance between lion and Dinanath at time $t$ is $\left[a-\dfrac{va}{u}\sin\left(\dfrac{ut}{a}\right)\right]$}
\opt{B}{If $a=10$ m, $u=5$ m/s and $v=10$ m/s then lion catches Dinanath after $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ s}
\opt{C}{Path followed by lion is circle}
\opt{D}{Path followed by lion is hyperbola}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=SI03-P1-PHY-S1-Q06, source={Score-I - Test 03 (07 Jan 2022)}, paper=1, qno=6, type=multi, subtopic={Projectile motion}, answer={B,D}, answer_src=key, difficulty=7, diff_parts={K2 S2 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: torque or moment, inertia of a square platform with given vertices | steps: find centre and side from vertices; moment of inertia about an axis through the centre; parallel axis; check | I: coordinates give the geometry in three dimensions}]
A square platform lies in horizontal X-Z plane such that its vertices are at $(8\,\mathrm{m}, 0\,\mathrm{m}, 16\,\mathrm{m})$, $(16\,\mathrm{m}, 0\,\mathrm{m}, 16\,\mathrm{m})$, $(8\,\mathrm{m}, 0\,\mathrm{m}, 24\,\mathrm{m})$ \& $(16\,\mathrm{m}, 0\,\mathrm{m}, 24\,\mathrm{m})$. A particle is projected with velocity $\left(v_2\hat i+25\hat j\right)$ m/s from origin w.r.t wind which blows at velocity $\left(v_1\hat k\right)$ m/s w.r.t. ground. At the same instant platform starts moving from rest with acceleration $\left(2\hat i+2.5\hat j\right)$ m s$^{-2}$. Acceleration due to gravity is $\left(-10\hat j\right)$ ms$^{-2}$. Choose the correct statement(s).
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{Possible value of $v_2$ if particle hits the platform is $6\leqslant v_2\leqslant10$}
\opt{B}{Possible value of $v_1$ if particle hits the platform is $4\leqslant v_1\leqslant6$}
\opt{C}{Possible time of flight of particle is 6 sec.}
\opt{D}{Possible time of flight of particle is 4 sec.}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=SI03-P2-PHY-S1-Q10, source={Score-I - Test 03 (07 Jan 2022)}, paper=2, qno=10, type=single, subtopic={1D and 2D motion}, answer={C}, answer_src=key, difficulty=3, diff_parts={K2 S1 I1 C0 F0}, diff_note={concepts: incorrect statement about velocity, acceleration vectors | steps: magnitude of derivative versus derivative of magnitude; choose incorrect relation}]
For a particle moving in space with velocity $\vec v$, which of the following is incorrect?
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$\left|\dfrac{d\vec v}{dt}\right|\geqslant\dfrac{d|\vec v|}{dt}$}
\opt{B}{$\displaystyle\int_0^t|\vec v|dt\geqslant\left|\int_0^t\vec v\,dt\right|$}
\opt{C}{$|\Delta\vec v|\leqslant\displaystyle\int_{t_1}^{t_2}|\vec a|dt$}
\opt{D}{$\dfrac{d|\vec v|}{dt}=\dfrac{d\vec v}{dt}\cdot\left(\dfrac{\vec v}{v}\right)$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=SI03-P2-PHY-S1-Q11, source={Score-I - Test 03 (07 Jan 2022)}, paper=2, qno=11, type=single, subtopic={Projectile motion}, answer={A}, answer_src=key, difficulty=5, diff_parts={K2 S2 I1 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: projectile landing on an inclined plane, horizontal launch | steps: resolve along and perpendicular to incline; time of flight; range along incline}]
In the given figure, the angle of inclination of the inclined plane is $30^\circ$. The horizontal velocity $V_0$ so that the particle hits the inclined plane perpendicularly is
\bfig{94.6}{SI03_p2_phy_s1_q11_A.png}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$v_0=\sqrt{\dfrac{2gH}{3}}$}
\opt{B}{$v_0=\sqrt{\dfrac{2gH}{7}}$}
\opt{C}{$v_0=\sqrt{\dfrac{gH}{5}}$}
\opt{D}{$v_0=\sqrt{\dfrac{gH}{7}}$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=SI03-P2-PHY-S1-Q12, source={Score-I - Test 03 (07 Jan 2022)}, paper=2, qno=12, type=single, subtopic={Relative motion}, answer={D}, answer_src=key, difficulty=5, diff_parts={K2 S2 I1 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: two boys running to meet, relative velocity direction | steps: boy at B moves perpendicular; the other chases along the line of sight; closing speed or time; evaluate}]
Two boys are standing at the points A and B on the ground, where $AB=a$. The boy at B starts running in a direction perpendicular to AB with velocity $v_1$. The boy at A starts running simultaneously with constant velocity $v$ and catches the other in time $t$ then $t$ is
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$\dfrac{a}{\sqrt{v^2+v_1^2}}$}
\opt{B}{$\dfrac{a}{v+v_1}$}
\opt{C}{$\dfrac{a}{v-v_1}$}
\opt{D}{$\dfrac{a}{\sqrt{v^2-v_1^2}}$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}

\begin{bankq}[id=SI11-P2-PHY-S1-Q06, source={Score-I - Test 11 (27 Feb 2022)}, paper=2, qno=6, type=multi, subtopic={1D and 2D motion}, answer={A,B,C,D}, answer_src=key, difficulty=6, diff_parts={K2 S2 I1 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: acceleration components, a particle on the path y = x^2/2 | steps: vx dvx/dt etc; y = x^2/2 gives vy = x vx and ay = vx^2 + x ax; initial speed 1 along x at origin; test each statement}, also_in={JEE Advanced (2021 Series) - Test 02 (04 Feb 2021) P2 Q6}]
Starting at time $t=0$ from the origin with speed 1 ms$^{-1}$, a particle follows a two-dimensional trajectory in the $x$-$y$ plane so that its coordinates are related by the equation $y=\dfrac{x^2}2$. The $x$ and $y$ components of its acceleration are denoted by $a_x$ and $a_y$, respectively. Then
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$a_x=1$ ms$^{-2}$ implies that when the particle is at the origin, $a_y=1$ ms$^{-2}$}
\opt{B}{$a_x=0$ implies $a_y=1$ ms$^{-2}$ at all times}
\opt{C}{at $t=0$, the particle's velocity points in the $x$-direction}
\opt{D}{$a_x=0$ implies that at $t=1$ s, the angle between the particle's velocity and the $x$ axis is $45^\circ$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}

\begin{bankq}[id=SI17-P1-PHY-S3-Q06, source={Score-I - Test 17 (17 Apr 2022)}, paper=1, qno=6, type=numerical, subtopic={1D and 2D motion}, answer={5.00}, answer_src=key, difficulty=7, diff_parts={K2 S2 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: radius of curvature of a particle moving on x = a t squared, y = b t cubed | steps: velocity and acceleration components at t = 1; radius of curvature = v^3/(a x v cross); equate to eta^3/12 | I: radius of curvature through cross product of velocity and acceleration}]

\begin{bankq}[id=SI18-P1-PHY-S1-Q01, source={Score-I - Test 18 (24 Apr 2022)}, paper=1, qno=1, type=single, subtopic={Relative motion}, answer={D}, answer_src=key, difficulty=4, diff_parts={K1 S2 I1 C1 F0}, diff_note={concepts: path of smoke relative to a moving train in still air | steps: particles fall at terminal speed so ground frame velocity is vertical plus horizontal drift zero; smoke leaves engine with train velocity then decelerates by air drag; trail shape}, also_in={JEE Advanced (2021 Series) - Test 01 (24 Jan 2021) P1 Q1}]

\begin{qoptions}

\opt{B}{Smoke trail would be at an acute angle to horizontal and smoke particles would be travelling along the smoke trail.}
\opt{C}{Smoke trail would be vertical but smoke particles would be travelling at an acute angle to the horizontal.}
\opt{D}{Smoke trail would be at an acute angle to horizontal but smoke particles would be travelling vertically.}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}

\begin{bankq}[id=SI31-P1-PHY-S1-Q05, source={Score-I - Test 31 (29 Dec 2022)}, paper=1, qno=5, type=multi, subtopic={Projectile motion}, answer={A,B,D}, answer_src=key, difficulty=6, diff_parts={K1 S2 I2 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: conditions for two shells fired at different times to collide in mid air | steps: equal horizontal positions u cos alpha t = u cos beta (t - T); equal vertical positions; deduce alpha larger and relations among t and T; check each | I: both coordinates must match at one instant}]
Two shells are fired from a cannon with a speed $u$ each, at angles of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ respectively to the horizontal. The time interval between the shots is $T$. They collide in mid-air after time $t$ from the first shot. Which of the following conditions must be satisfied?
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$\alpha>\beta$}
\opt{B}{$t\cos\alpha=(t-T)\cos\beta$}
\opt{C}{$(t-T)\cos\alpha=t\cos\beta$}
\opt{D}{$(u\sin\alpha)t-\tfrac12gt^2=(u\sin\beta)(t-T)-\tfrac12g(t-T)^2$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
